data.title: Middle East Eye: Watch: Gaza declares meningitis alert as health ministry blames Israeli restrictions
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Watch: Gaza declares meningitis alert as health ministry blames Israeli restrictions
Gaza’s health ministry has issued an "epidemiological alert" across the territory, warning that a "shocking" increase in meningitis infections puts hundreds of thousands of lives at risk, particularly children.
The ministry urged the World Health Organization and Unicef to launch an emergency response.
Dr Nidal Ghunaim, deputy director general of primary healthcare for public health, reported 272 cases in October. He described the figure as more than eight times the usual monthly average of 30 to 50.
Meningitis has killed 15 people this year, Ghunaim said, including five during the surge from August to October.
The ministry described the outbreak as an "inevitable result of the destruction of infrastructure, overcrowding of shelters, mixing of drinking water with sewage, and the disaster being exacerbated by flooding due to rain".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Morning update
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Morning update
Good morning Middle East Eye readers,
Here are the latest developments:
An Israeli attack on an apartment in Gaza City has killed a senior Palestinian security official alongside his wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15. According to the interior ministry, the man was identified as the director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, 47. This marks the second killing of a security official in Gaza in less than 24 hours, with the previous attack killing director-general of the Internal Security Service, Naim Mohammed Abu Nahl.
Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said that Tehran is not concerned about the US naval blockade, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported. He indicated the country's self-reliance with the increase of cargo clearance through its non-southern borders and added that reserves of strategic goods remain strong.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said that two "offending" oil tankers on the southern and eastern coasts of the Strait of Hormuz suffered explosions. "These tankers, believing they were secretly trying to pass through the fake Strait of Hormuz route, were prevented from passing by naval mines, causing a massive explosion and fire," it said in a statement.
The Saudi-led coalition's spokesperson said in a post on X that it targeted "operational capabilities" at Yemen's Hodeidah port. Additionally, Turki al-Maliki added that a number of targets in northern Yemen's Saada and Amran governorates were destroyed.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura, located in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. The coalition's spokesperson Turki al-Maliki indicated that a number of fragments had fallen as a result of the interception, with no casualties reported in the initial assessment.
A US poll shows Trump's approval at 37 percent, with strong disapproval over his handling of the Iran war.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Why Israel should be afraid of the ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar
data.author: Jonathan Cook
data.summary:
Why Israel should be afraid of the ICJ genocide ruling against Myanmar
Submitted by
Jonathan Cook
on
Tue, 11/24/2026 - 10:57
The court's finding against Myanmar undercuts each of Israel's defences over Gaza, and exposes the western states that cheered one verdict while arming the other genocide
Pro-Palestinian protesters demonstrate outside the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague, on 24 May, 2024 (Reuters)
Off
There are many reasons why Israel will be deeply worried by the International Court of Justice's finding on 19 November that the military junta in Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority nearly a decade ago.
The president of the world's highest court, Yuji Iwasawa, concluded that Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya population and tried to hide its crimes through "extensive destruction of evidence".
During so-called "clearance operations" in 2017, Myanmar's security forces from the Buddhist-majority state of Myanmar killed at least 10,000 Rohingya, a Muslim minority, and drove more than 700,000 from their homes in northern Rakhine state. Most found refuge in Bangladesh.
Entire villages were erased, evidence destroyed by burning bodies and bulldozing sites, and the Rohingya subjected to campaigns of rape and sexual violence. Myanmar failed to prosecute the perpetrators.
So what are the implications for another prominent genocide case being considered by the ICJ, this one brought against Israel by South Africa, and backed by more than a dozen other countries, including Ireland, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands?
Back in January 2024, just weeks into Israel's onslaught in Gaza, the World Court found a "plausible risk" that Palestinians there were being subjected to genocide.
It also imposed a series of provisional measures on Israel to ensure its military did not commit genocidal acts, that aid was allowed in, that all incitement stopped, and that the destruction of evidence was prevented. Israe

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli minister calls Palestinians and Muslims 'camel riders' and 'barbarians'
data.author: Sondos Asem
data.summary:
Israeli minister calls Palestinians and Muslims 'camel riders' and 'barbarians'
The outgoing Israeli minister of heritage, Amichai Eliyahu, called Palestinians and Muslims "camel riders" and "barbarians" during a speech in parliament on Monday, amid escalating racist abuse against Palestinian citizens of Israel.
"Your education needs fixing. You need to be educated- not here in Israel, but everywhere in the world," Eliyahu said during a discussion on crime in Palestinian society in Israel.
"You destroyed the Twin Towers, you are destroying Europe, you make a mess everywhere you touch," said the minister, who previously suggested dropping an atomic bomb on the Gaza Strip.
"If you don't change, your children will die, and it's not because of us, it's because of you," added Eliyahu, a member of National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party.
Since Ben Gvir took over the ministry in late 2022, which oversees the police, crime in Palestinian society in Israel has skyrocketed. Palestinian leaders have accused Ben Gvir and the police force of allowing criminal organisations to operate unchecked.

UN human rights chief Volker Turk warned on Wednesday of a growing risk of further atrocity crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, urging all states to take immediate action to prevent them.
Turk cited inflammatory statements by senior Israeli officials advocating annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment, alongside increasingly widespread and systematic violations against Palestinians.
“Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes – war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide – has been appalling,” he said in a statement.
The UN rights chief said his office had repeatedly warned that Israel’s actions in Gaza posed a “real threat to the continued existence” of Palestinians as a group.
“Our warnings have not been heeded, and atrocity crimes continue to recur,” he added.

Amnesty says Palestinian women and girls bear crushing toll of Israel’s genocide
Amnesty International said on Wednesday that Israel continues to inflict devastating harm on Palestinian women and girls in Gaza as part of its ongoing genocide, despite the October 2025 ceasefire.
In a new 135-page report, the rights group documented the killing, maiming, forced displacement, unlawful detention and starvation of women and girls, as well as the deliberate denial of essential healthcare, including reproductive care, between October 2023 and October 2026.
“This new report sheds light on the profound gendered dimensions of Israel’s genocide, providing new details about the brutal harms inflicted on women and girls that continue to devastate their lives and cause agonizing suffering despite the so-called ceasefire,” said Agnes Callamard, Amnesty’s secretary general.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Tortured into confessing: Report exposes abusive Israeli interrogation of Palestinians
data.author: Elis Gjevori
data.summary:
Tortured into confessing: Report exposes abusive Israeli interrogation of Palestinians
Submitted by
Elis Gjevori
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 13:09
More than 1,680 interrogation torture complaints led to five criminal investigations, all closed without indictments
Palestinians released from Israeli prisons are examined by medics at the Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital in Deir el-Balah in the central Gaza Strip on 10 April 2025 (Eyad Baba/AFP)
Off
In 2021, Israeli police arrested a Palestinian man known as R, who after multiple rounds of torture, signed a confession document for a crime he did not commit.
He is one of hundreds of Palestinians featured in a report by the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI) who faced criminal proceedings on the basis of confessions extracted under duress.
The man, whose name was withheld for fear of reprisals, spent months in prison before video footage showed he had been nowhere near the scene of the crime he was accused of.
Before that video came to light, R repeatedly tried to withdraw his confession to the unspecified crime but was tortured by Shin Bet officials regardless.
He and his brother, who had also faced charges, eventually secured acquittals and their release.
Theirs was a rare case of acquittal within an Israeli justice system where torture, sexual assault, rape and inhuman treatment have become normalised, according to multiple reports from human rights organisations and the UN.
In its report, PCATI profiled 42 cases it had filed over the past decade on behalf of Palestinians who reported torture during Shin Bet interrogations.
In 33 of those cases, Palestinian detainees confessed under torture during or after questioning.
Israeli courts only recognised four of those confessions as false, despite interrogators using torture on the detainees.
The report describes how a confession extracted under duress can make its way into a criminal case.

data.title: Middle East Eye: More than a third of Muslim students experience Islamophobia at UK universities, report finds
data.author: Areeb Ullah
data.summary:
More than a third of Muslim students experience Islamophobia at UK universities, report finds
Submitted by
Areeb Ullah
on
Thu, 11/19/2026 - 17:12
Students surveyed by the Federation of Student Islamic Societies found that Muslim students from Russell Group universities faced more discrimination
Students hold a banner listing the names of people killed in Gaza during a pro-Palestine demonstration in London in October 2025 (Reuters)
Off
More than one in three Muslim students in the UK have experienced Islamophobia at university, with many facing abuse, threats and religious discrimination, according to a new report by the Federation of Student Islamic Societies (Fosis).
The report, titled "Belonging in Question", found that 38 percent of Muslim students surveyed had experienced Islamophobia on campus, while 68 percent of those affected said they did not feel able to report what had happened to them.
Rahma Hegy, Fosis vice-president for student affairs, said Muslim students continued to make significant contributions to university life and wider British society, despite feeling unwelcome on campus.
"Many [students] tell us they do not feel they belong on the very campuses meant to include them," Hegy told Middle East Eye.
"They face discrimination, and too often they stay quiet because they do not expect anyone to be held accountable."
Hegy said the lack of accountability was among the organisation's greatest concerns and urged universities, student unions and the government to act on it.
The findings are based on responses from 715 students across 63 higher education institutions in the UK, making it one of the largest recent surveys of Muslim students' experiences at British universities.
Students described a range of incidents, including being spat at, receiving death threats and having urine thrown at them while wearing the hijab.
Others reported being excluded from laboratory sessions after requesting time to attend Friday prayers, being told to remove their hijab

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel kills security official and family in Gaza, as UN warns of 'real threat' to Palestinian existence
data.author: Alex MacDonald
data.summary:
Israel kills security official and family in Gaza, as UN warns of 'real threat' to Palestinian existence
Submitted by
Alex MacDonald
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 12:11
Killing of official in northern Gaza marks second deadly Israeli attack on security personnel in less than 24 hours and is condemned as an attempt to 'spread chaos' by the Interior Ministry
Mojahed Abu al-Ouf is consoled by his aunt at Al-Shifa Hospital as he bids farewell to his parents and two sisters after they were killed in an overnight Israeli air strike in Gaza City on 25 November 2026 (Omar al-Qattaa/AFP)
Off
A senior security official, his wife and his two daughters were killed in an Israeli air strike in Gaza overnight on Tuesday, as the UN warned of a "real threat" to Palestinian existence.
The attack on the apartment in Gaza City killed the director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, alongside his wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15.
It marked the second killing of a security official in Gaza in less than 24 hours, with the previous attack killing Naim Mohammed Abu Nahl, the director-general of the Internal Security Service.
